thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: dynamic-batcher-service triggered an incident (PD-INC-4832). Alert: error_rate >= 2% for 5m. Auto-page to on-call.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty page fired to schedule 'sre-oncall' (sev: P1). Incident link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-INC-4832

Tayler_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Starting triage. :white_check_mark:

maria: seeing a spike of 5xx from the canary revision (rev=canary-dynamic-v3). p95 latency up from 180ms -> 1.2s. Which rollout enabled dynamic_batching?

eng-release: that was the staged rollout from this morning, dynamic_batching toggled on via configmap in canary group at 09:12 UTC.

maria: logs show a lot of "queue timeout" and "batch overflow". here's a snippet: 
```
2023-11-14T09:18:02Z ERROR request_handler.go:312 request_id=abc123 status=503 reason="batch overflow" batch_size=128 timeout=1000ms
2023-11-14T09:18:04Z WARN kvcache.go:87 lease_miss=true shard=4
```

Tayler_oncall: good, can you run quick K8s and rollout checks? Also confirm customer impact (any elevated alerts from enterprise accounts)?

maria: running `kubectl -n inference get deploy -o wide` now. canary pods are at 3/5 ready. Some pods are CrashLoopBackOff.

maria: command used:
```
kubectl -n inference describe deploy dynamic-model-canary | sed -n '1,120p'
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/dynamic-model-canary -c runtime --tail=200
```

devx: looks like the canary's new batcher is holding requests until batch is full, causing head-of-line blocking during low concurrency flows. We saw similar during local stress tests but not at this combination of seq len + concurrency.

ops-bot: Incident timeline updated. Current best-effort mitigation: reduce canary traffic to 0% using rollout weights.

Tayler_oncall: do that now. eng-release, can you flip traffic weight back to stable?

eng-release: executing: `rctl rollout set-weight dynamic-service --canary 0 --stable 100`

eng-release: done. Verified weights changed. Stable pods receiving 100% traffic. Canary pods should drain.

pagerduty-bot: PD note: incident updated. Auto-escalation timer paused due to ack.

maria: after weight shift, error rate dropped to 0.3% within 90s. p95 back to ~210ms. Customer Success says no new tickets but one large account (AcmeCorp) reported intermittent errors at 09:20 UTC — they will follow up if they see more.

customer-success: AcmeCorp sent a message, they saw a brief increase in failed document uploads during the window. We're monitoring.

sre-lead: good catch. For immediate mitigation: rollback canary image to v2 and disable dynamic_batching flag in configmap for canary group; keep canary scaled down until we complete deeper analysis.

eng-release: scheduling rollback: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/dynamic-model-canary runtime=registry/redwood/dynamic:v2 --record` and `kubectl -n inference patch configmap dynamic-batcher-cfg -p '{"data":{"dynamic_batching":"false"}}'`

eng-release: rollback applied and configmap toggled. Canary pods restarting to v2.

maria: monitoring metrics... error rate trending down to baseline. No further 503s in logs after new pods stabilized.

Tayler_oncall: handing off to SRE lead for post-incident analysis and RCA. SRE-lead you'll take lead; I'll remain available for follow-ups.

sre-lead: taking ownership for RCA and follow-up. Assigning postmortem. Preliminary notes: likely bug in batch assembly logic interacting with KV-cache misses under low concurrency -> causing oversized batch waits and timeouts.

sre-lead: immediate action items: (1) block dynamic_batching flag from going to canary without gating tests that simulate low-concurrency long-sequence workloads; (2) add circuit-breaker on batch timeout to fail fast; (3) add telemetry to measure batch fill latency and drop rates.

devx: will open a PR to add unit/integration tests for low-concurrency scenarios and add a config gate in the operator to prevent rollout until validation passes.

eng-release: opening rollback post-deploy ticket and notifying release manager. Also adding a temporary alert suppression for the canary group to avoid alert spam while we investigate.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty update: incident PD-INC-4832 marked as mitigated by on-call at 09:28 UTC. Incident will be closed after postmortem created.

incident-bot: Created incident doc at /incidents/PD-INC-4832-dynamic-batcher-canary-autopage with timeline and artifacts.

customer-success: I'll email AcmeCorp with a summary and offer to run a replay of their failing requests against stable to confirm no data loss.

Tayler_oncall: thanks team. Quick notes for handoff: owner=sre-lead, severity=P1->mitigated, impact=brief 503 spike affecting a subset of canary traffic and one large customer (no data loss known). Next steps: RCA + tests + deploy gating.

sre-lead: assigning owners: devx -> tests, eng-runtime -> circuit-breaker + telemetry, eng-release -> release gating. Targeting preliminary postmortem in 48h.

maria: adding logs and perf snapshots to the incident doc. If anyone has additional traces (zipkin/tempo) drop them in the doc.

Tayler_oncall: handoff complete. I'm going offline, reachable if needed. :handshake:

eng-release: note: we'll also schedule a canary replay during low-traffic window to validate fixes before re-enabling dynamic_batching.

sre-lead: thanks all. Closing thread here, will update incident doc with RCA and action items.
